memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But if, when the priest examines it, the mould has not spread in the fabric, the woven or knitted material, or the leather article, he shall order that the spoiled article be washed. Then he is to isolate it for another seven days. After the article has been washed, the priest is to examine it again, and if the mould has not changed its appearance, even though it has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it, whether the mould has affected one side or the other." - Lev 13:53-55 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a sobering detail. The article was washed. And after washing, it still had to be examined — and if nothing had changed, it was burned anyway.

Washing was not automatically enough.

This speaks to something we all know quietly. We can go through the outward motions of dealing with sin without anything actually changing. We apologise without repenting. We confess the same thing for the tenth year running with no intention of doing differently. We attend, we sing, we pray the words — and afterwards we are exactly as we were.

Isaiah records God's own weariness with this: these people come near to me with their mouth and honour me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Isa 29:13). Jesus quoted that verse to the religious leaders of His day (Matt 15:8).

The test here was change. Had the appearance altered? Was anything different?

So it is worth asking honestly: in the areas I regularly bring to God, is anything actually changing? Or have I settled into a comfortable cycle of confession without transformation?

God is not after the ritual. He is after us. And He is more than able to do the deeper work if we will let Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you confessed something repeatedly without any real change?
2. Is your repentance producing difference, or only relief?
3. What deeper work might God want to do in that area?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not want a religion of words without change. Do the deeper work in me, and make my repentance real rather than routine. Amen.
